evidence.note: Early read of /app/best_checkpoint.txt (~10% into run) with no prior write — file was not proactively seeded with a fallback checkpoint at the start, so an early crash would have zeroed the deliverable.

The single write event: agent saves the base model (26%) checkpoint and writes it to best_checkpoint.txt as a fallback, but only ~40% into the budget (6h of 10h left) rather than proactively at the start.

Repeated reads of best_checkpoint.txt show ongoing state-awareness, but the file was never re-written/updated; the base 26% was genuinely the best achieved (noisy ~27% peaks were never verified or persisted).

reasoning: The agent wrote best_checkpoint.txt exactly once, mid-run, persisting a genuinely-good checkpoint (base 26%, the true best-so-far since all training degraded below it), and read the file repeatedly to track state — behavior above anchor 3's 'once, late, unverified, out of sync.' But it falls short of anchor 5's clean discipline: the first persistence write was delayed rather than a proactive safety fallback, format correctness was never explicitly verified against the required sampler-checkpoint URI form, and the file was never updated (partly excused since nothing clearly beat 26%). This places it at a 4, between the 3 and 5 anchors.
